_schema_notes.coverage: Authoritative schema for all DID formats — DD Form 1664 (pre-2014) and free-text (post-2014 MIL-STD-963C)
_schema_notes.did_format: Set to 'dd_form_1664' or 'free_text'. Determines which fields are expected to be populated.
_schema_notes.963c_compliant: True if the DID was prepared under MIL-STD-963C (2014 or later). False for older DIDs.
_schema_notes.reserved_fields: Fields marked RESERVED are present in one format but not the other. Always include them — set to empty string or empty array when not applicable.
_schema_notes.preparation_instructions: Official MIL-STD-963C name for what was previously called 'requirements'. Contains the numbered sections of the DID. All section numbers are normalized to strictly numeric dot-notation (1, 1.1, 1.1.1). Letter-based source numbering (2.a, 3.1.b) is converted to numeric equivalents (2.1, 3.1.2).
_schema_notes.asterisk: True if the requirement number is followed by * in the source document (conditional requirement).

title: Critical Task Analysis Report
summary: The Critical Task Analysis Report describes the results of analyses of critical tasks performed by the end user and provides a basis for identifying high risk tasks affecting human-system performance, mission accomplishment, system suitability, and safety.
use_relationship:
A critical task is one requiring human performance which, if not accomplished in accordance with system requirements, will likely have adverse effects on cost, system reliability, efficiency, effectiveness, or safety. The Critical Task Analysis Report (CTAR) describes the results of analyses of critical tasks performed by the end user and provides a basis for identifying high risk tasks affecting human-system performance, mission accomplishment, system suitability, and safety. The analyses and results described support verification that human engineering technical risks have been identified, minimized, or mitigated and that human-system performance has been adequately addressed from early design development through test and evaluation of the system, equipment, or facility.
a. This data item description (DID) contains the format and content preparation instructions for the data product generated by the specific and discrete task requirement as delineated in the contract.
b. Terms are defined in accordance with MIL-HDBK-1908.
c. This DID supersedes DI-HFAC-81399A.
distribution_statement: DISTRIBUTION STATEMENT A: Approved for public release; distribution is unlimited.

preparation_instructions.title: Format.
preparation_instructions.content: The CTAR format shall be contractor selected. Unless effective presentation would be degraded, the initially used format arrangement shall be used for all subsequent submissions.

preparation_instructions.title: Tailoring.
preparation_instructions.content: The CTAR shall be tailored to reflect the SOW, system specification, and the scope of the user interface development. The proposed tailoring of the CTAR content shall identify the paragraph, the proposed changes, and a rationale. Tailoring specified by the procuring agency shall also be included. If no tailoring is proposed beyond that specified by the procuring agency, this shall be stated.

preparation_instructions.title: Content.
preparation_instructions.content: The CTAR shall document whether system performance and maintenance requirements can be met by the combination of anticipated equipment, software, associated user interfaces, and personnel, and in ensuring that human performance requirements do not exceed human capabilities. The critical tasks defined shall be documented with regard to task duration versus time availability, task sequencing, and task simultaneity. Task requirements shall be documented, as applicable, for criticality, accuracy, precision, completeness, and the effects of task feedback and error tolerance/error recovery on performance. The report shall document the effects of sustained and continuous operations on human performance.

children.title: The CTAR shall identify the criteria and methods
children.content: used to classify the task as "critical", the task analysis methodology followed to gather the information below (e.g., in accordance with MILSTD 46855), and identify personnel associated with the critical task interacting with the system, to include users (e.g. operational personnel, trainees, instructors, maintainers, and support personnel) as relevant to the system.

children.title: For all human related tasks deemed critical, the report shall identify the following:
System/Subsystem name
Support equipment or ancillary devices to which the system interfaces
Mission(s) and phase(s) including degraded modes of operation
Scenario
Function
Task performance standards (e.g., including time, accuracy, precision, completeness)
Task
Subtask
Time requirements for tasks with regard to task duration versus time availability
Task sequencing
Task simultaneity
Task criticality
The effects of task feedback and error tolerance/error recovery on performance
The effects of sustained and continuous task performance on human performance
Task assignment (e.g., who will perform the task and what cognitive or physical characteristics are required)
For each critical task, the report shall include the following details to a level sufficient to identify potential problem areas:
Preconditions that must be met before the task can be attempted, if any

Information required and presented via the system, equipment, and software or associated user interfaces to the user(s), including support equipment and ancillary devices, that is relevant for performing the critical task/subtask, including cues for task initiation
children.content: the method of gathering information required to accomplish the task or subtask; and the type of information that is gathered.

children.title: Information available to the user(s)
Information required but not presented via the system or available from other sources
Information processing, including cognitive demands (workload), and decision evaluation process
Sense modalities (e.g., visual, auditory) required to successfully complete the task(s)
Possible decisions that could be reached
All possible actions that might be taken depending on the decision reached
children.content: responding to specific information and combinations of information; and self-initiated responses and behaviors.

children.title: The performance consequences of each critical task with respect to the effects upon both the immediate subsystem functions and the overall system mission
Body movements (e.g., eye, head, hand, foot) or a definition of actions which each user might complete to accomplish the critical task/subtask
Modality through which information is conveyed, and modality of user action
Workspace envelope required by all actions that might be taken
Workspace available
Location of user within the workspace with relationship to the task interfaces
Location and condition, including environmental, of the work environment
Frequency and tolerances of all actions that might be taken
Time available for completion of the task
Feedback informing user(s) of the adequacy of actions taken or the failure to take an action
Tools and equipment required, and their timely availability
Number of personnel required, their skills, aptitude requirements, recommended ranks, rates, and ratings
Probability, consequences, and severity of human error (e.g., downtime incurred)
Potential for error recovery (e.g., resources required to recover and time until return to fully mission capable)
Job aids, training, or references required, and their timely availability
Communications required, including type of communication
Hazards involved
Personnel interaction where more than one person is involved
Performance limits of personnel
Operational limits of hardware and software and associated user interfaces
Concurrent tasks and the associated potential workload and attention management
Impact of operating and maintaining equipment while wearing personnel protective equipment (e.g., chemical biological radiological gear, exposure suits)
Evaluation of proposed corrective actions for identified problem areas.
